definition: The algorithm the browser uses to choose one value when several declarations target the same property on the same element: origin and importance, inline styles, layers, specificity, then order of appearance.
When no declaration targets an inherited property such as `color` or `font-family`, the element takes its parent's computed value; non-inherited properties fall back to their initial value instead.
A selector's weight, counted as three separate numbers (IDs; classes, attributes and pseudo-classes; types and pseudo-elements) and compared column by column, never added together.
A pseudo-class that matches like `:is()` but always contributes zero specificity, which makes it ideal for resets and base styles that components should override easily.
A pseudo-class that matches any selector in its list and takes the specificity of its most specific argument; it uses a forgiving selector list, so one invalid argument doesn't drop the rule.
A named group of rules created with `@layer`. Later-declared layers beat earlier ones before specificity is compared, and unlayered styles beat all layers for normal declarations.
A property whose name starts with two dashes, such as `--track-color`, read with `var()`. It inherits by default and is substituted where it is used, at computed-value time.
What happens when a `var()` substitution produces a value the property can't use: the property behaves as unset, taking its inherited or initial value rather than an earlier declaration.
An at-rule that registers a custom property with a syntax, an inheritance flag and an initial value, so the browser can validate it and interpolate it in transitions and animations.
Native syntax for writing rules inside other rules, where `&` stands for the parent selector. It works on selectors, not text, so it can't build BEM class names the way Sass does.
A relational pseudo-class that matches an element when the relative selector inside it finds a match, letting a parent or earlier sibling be styled by its descendants or later siblings.
The starting size of a flex item along the main axis, before leftover space is shared by `flex-grow` or a shortfall is taken back by `flex-shrink`.
The default `min-width: auto` of flex and grid items, which stops them shrinking below their content. Setting `min-width: 0` lets long text truncate instead of overflowing.
A grid property that names regions of the grid with strings, one per row, so you can place items by name and rearrange the layout by redrawing the strings.
A keyword for `repeat()` that creates as many tracks as fit and collapses the empty ones, so a few items stretch to fill the row; `auto-fill` keeps empty tracks instead.
The `subgrid` value for `grid-template-rows` or `grid-template-columns`, which makes a nested grid use the tracks it spans in its parent, so content aligns across sibling components.
An intrinsic sizing keyword that sizes an element to its max-content width, capped at the available space, so a block can hug its content without overflowing.
A math function that returns a preferred value held between a minimum and a maximum, written `clamp(MIN, PREFERRED, MAX)`. It equals `max(MIN, min(PREFERRED, MAX))`.
An `@container` rule that applies styles based on the size or style of an ancestor container rather than the viewport, so a component adapts to the slot it sits in.
Units such as `cqi` and `cqb` that equal 1% of the nearest size container's inline or block size, falling back to small viewport units when no container exists.
Font sizes that change continuously with available width, usually written as `clamp()` with a rem minimum, a linear preferred value combining rem and `vw` or `cqi`, and a rem maximum.
Properties named by text flow instead of physical sides, such as `margin-inline-start` and `inline-size`, so layouts mirror correctly in right-to-left languages like Arabic.
A color function using perceptual lightness, chroma and hue, so colors with equal lightness look equally light. It can also express colors beyond the sRGB gamut.
A way to derive a color from another by unpacking its channels with `from`, as in `oklch(from var(--brand) calc(l - 0.1) c h)`, and changing only what you need.
A color function that returns its first value when the element's used color scheme is light and its second when it's dark. It needs `color-scheme` to allow dark.
A pseudo-class that matches a focused element only when the browser judges a focus indicator useful, such as keyboard focus or any text field, but not a mouse click on a button.
An at-rule that defines the styles an element transitions from when it is first rendered or goes from `display: none` to shown, enabling entry transitions in CSS alone.
An animation created by `document.startViewTransition()`: the browser snapshots the old and new states of a DOM update and animates between them through pseudo-elements you can style.
A CSS animation whose progress follows a scroll timeline, set with `animation-timeline: scroll()` or `view()`, instead of elapsed time.
The final rendering stage, where painted layers are assembled on the GPU. Changes to `transform` and `opacity` can often be handled here alone, skipping layout and paint.
